1.1: After Saul died, David had just come back from fighting the Amalekites and had been chillin' in Ziklag for two days.
1.2: On the third day, a man came from Saul's camp, lookin' rough—clothes torn, dust all over him. He fell to the ground in front of David.
1.3: David asked, 'Where you from?' The man said, 'I made it out of Israel's camp alive.'
1.4: David asked, 'What happened? Tell me everything.' The man said, 'Israel got wiped out. A lot of people got killed. Saul and Jonathan are dead.'
1.5: David asked, 'How you know for sure that Saul and Jonathan are dead?'
1.6: The man said, 'I was on Mount Gilboa, and I saw Saul leanin' on his spear with enemy chariots and soldiers closin' in on him.'
1.7: He looked back and saw me, called me over. I said, 'Here I am.'
1.8: Saul asked, 'Who you wit'?' and I told him, 'I'm an Amalekite.'
1.9: Then he said, 'Kill me. I'm barely holdin' on, and I don't wanna go out like this.'
1.10: So I did it. I put him out his misery 'cause I knew he wasn't gon' make it. Then I took his crown and his bracelet, and I brought 'em to you.
1.11: David tore his clothes in grief, and all his men did too.
1.12: They mourned, cried, and fasted till sundown, grieving over Saul, Jonathan, and all the fallen Israelites.
1.13: David asked the young man, 'Where you from again?' He said, 'I'm an Amalekite, born to a foreigner.'
1.14: David snapped, 'You wasn't scared to kill the Lord's anointed?!'
1.15: Then David told one of his men, 'Handle him.' And they took him out.
1.16: David told the young man, 'You brought this on yourself. You said with your own mouth that you killed the Lord's anointed.'
1.17: David wrote a song for Saul and Jonathan, mourning their deaths.
1.18: He told Judah to learn it, callin' it The Song of the Bow. (It was written in The Book of Jasher.)
1.19: The glory of Israel is gone, fallen on the heights! How the mighty have fallen!
1.20: Don't let the Philistines in Gath hear it! Don't spread the news in Ashkelon, or their women will celebrate.
1.21: May Mount Gilboa never see rain again—Saul's shield was tossed away there, no longer anointed with oil.
1.22: Jonathan's bow stayed sharp, Saul's sword never missed.
1.23: Saul and Jonathan—beloved in life, inseparable in death. Faster than eagles, stronger than lions!
1.24: Daughters of Israel, cry for Saul! He gave y'all luxury and gold.
1.25: How the mighty have fallen! Jonathan—killed on the battlefield.
1.26: I'm hurtin' for you, my brother Jonathan. Your love was real, deeper than a woman's love.
1.27: How the mighty have fallen! Weapons of war gone.

2.1: After all that went down, David asked The Most High, 'Should I go up to one of Judah's cities?' And The Most High said, 'Yeah, go up.' David asked, 'Where exactly?' And He said, 'Hebron.'
2.2: So David packed up and went to Hebron, takin' both his wives—Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
2.3: David also brought all his people who was rollin' with him, and they moved their families into the towns around Hebron.
2.4: Then the men of Judah came through and made David king over Judah. They also told him, 'Yo, the men of Jabesh-Gilead the ones who buried Saul.'
2.5: David sent a message to them, sayin', 'Y'all blessed by The Most High for what y'all did—showin' love to Saul and givin' him a proper burial.'
2.6: 'May The Most High show y'all love and truth for that. And I'ma do right by y'all too, 'cause y'all handled that like real ones.'
2.7: 'So be strong, stand tall. Saul is gone, but Judah made me king now.'
2.8: But Abner, son of Ner—who was Saul's top general—took Saul's son Ishbosheth and moved him to Mahanaim.
2.9: Then he made him king over Gilead, Ashurites, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin—basically all of Israel.
2.10: Ishbosheth was 40 years old when he started ruling over Israel. He only lasted two years. Meanwhile, Judah was ridin' with David.
2.11: David reigned over Judah from Hebron for seven years and six months.
2.12: One day, Abner and Ishbosheth's crew left Mahanaim and pulled up to Gibeon.
2.13: Joab, Zeruiah's son, and David's crew pulled up too. They met at the pool of Gibeon—sittin' on opposite sides, just starin' at each other.
2.14: Abner was like, 'Let's have some of these young dudes get up and scrap for us.' Joab was like, 'Bet. Let's do it.'
2.15: So twelve of Ishbosheth's guys from Benjamin and twelve of David's squad got up.
2.16: They squared up, grabbed each other, and straight-up stabbed each other at the same time. They all dropped dead. That's why they called that place 'The Field of Sharp Swords' in Gibeon.
2.17: After that, a wild fight broke out, and David's crew beat Ishbosheth's squad down.
2.18: Now Joab, Abishai, and Asahel—three brothers—were out there. Asahel was quick, dude ran like a gazelle.
2.19: He chased after Abner, not switchin' lanes or slowin' down, locked in on him.
2.20: Abner looked back and said, 'Yo, that you, Asahel?' Asahel was like, 'Yeah, it's me.'
2.21: Abner told him, 'Fall back, bro. Go take somebody else's gear.' But Asahel wasn't lettin' up.
2.22: Abner said again, 'Bruh, stop! I don't wanna kill you. I can't face your brother Joab if I do.'
2.23: But Asahel didn't listen. So Abner hit him with the back end of his spear, right in the gut. Spear went straight through, and dude dropped on the spot. Everybody who saw him dead like that just stopped in their tracks.
2.24: Joab and Abishai kept chasin' Abner till sundown. They caught up with him near Giah, on the way to the Gibeon desert.
2.25: The Benjamites regrouped behind Abner, formed up, and took their stand on a hill.
2.26: Abner called out to Joab, 'Bruh, how long we gon' do this? You know it's only gon' end bad. Call your people off.'
2.27: Joab said, 'Man, if you ain't say nothin', my guys would've chased y'all till morning.'
2.28: Then Joab blew the horn, and everybody stopped fightin'. No more chasin', no more beefin'.
2.29: Abner and his men walked all night, crossed the Jordan, and made it back to Mahanaim.
2.30: Joab stopped the chase, regrouped his people, and counted up—nineteen of his men and Asahel were dead.
2.31: But they took out 360 men from Abner's squad.
2.32: They picked up Asahel's body and buried him in Bethlehem. Then Joab and his crew marched all night and made it back to Hebron by sunrise.

3.1: That war between Saul's people and David's people dragged on for a long time. But David kept gettin' stronger, while Saul's house kept fallin' off.
3.2: While in Hebron, David had some sons. His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam from Jezreel.
3.3: His second was Chileab, by Abigail—Nabal's widow from Carmel. Third was Absalom, son of Maacah, Talmai's daughter, the king of Geshur.
3.4: Fourth was Adonijah, son of Haggith. Fifth was Shephatiah, son of Abital.
3.5: Sixth was Ithream, by Eglah, another one of David's wives. All these kids was born while David was in Hebron.
3.6: During the war between Saul's house and David's, Abner was out here tryin' to secure his spot in Saul's camp.
3.7: Now, Saul had a concubine named Rizpah, daughter of Aiah. Ishbosheth came at Abner like, 'Why you messin' with my father's woman?'
3.8: That set Abner off. He said, 'Bruh, you really think I'm out here playin' games? I been holdin' it down for your daddy's house, his people, and his friends. I could've flipped on you anytime, but I didn't. And you gon' come at me over this?'
3.9: 'Man, may God deal with me if I don't do what He promised David—'
3.10: 'Move this whole kingdom from Saul's people to David's, from Dan to Beersheba.'
3.11: Ishbosheth ain't say nothin' after that 'cause he knew Abner wasn't one to play with.
3.12: So Abner sent messengers to David like, 'Aye, who really runnin' this land? Let's make a deal, and I'ma bring all Israel over to you.'
3.13: David was like, 'Bet, we can do that. But first, I need you to bring Michal, Saul's daughter, when you come to see me.'
3.14: David also sent word to Ishbosheth, sayin', 'Run me my wife Michal—I put in work for her, paid for her with Philistine foreskins.'
3.15: So Ishbosheth made her husband, Paltiel, give her up.
3.16: Dude was heartbroken, followed her cryin' all the way to Bahurim, till Abner turned around and said, 'Man, go home.' And he did.
3.17: Abner started talkin' to the Israelite elders, sayin', 'Y'all been wantin' David as king for a minute.'
3.18: 'Well, it's time! The Most High already said David is the one who's gonna save Israel from the Philistines and all our enemies.'
3.19: He also hollered at the tribe of Benjamin, then went down to Hebron to talk to David about all this.
3.20: Abner pulled up to Hebron with twenty of his people. David threw a big feast for them.
3.21: Then Abner told David, 'I'ma bring all of Israel to you, so you can rule over everything like you always wanted.' David let Abner leave in peace.
3.22: Right after that, Joab and David's men came back from a raid, bringin' a whole lot of loot. Abner wasn't there 'cause David had already sent him off in peace.
3.23: When Joab got back, folks told him, 'Yo, Abner came to the king, and David let him leave on good terms.'
3.24: Joab was heated. He went straight to David like, 'Bruh, what did you just do?! Abner was just here, and you let him leave?'
3.25: 'You know Abner only came to spy on you, right? He just tryna peep your moves!'
3.26: Joab left David and secretly sent messengers to bring Abner back, but David ain't know about it.
3.27: When Abner got back to Hebron, Joab pulled him to the side like, 'Let's talk in private.' Then he straight-up stabbed him in the gut—killed him right there, tryna get revenge for his brother Asahel.
3.28: When David heard about it, he said, 'I ain't got nothin' to do with this. My kingdom clean from this murder forever.'
3.29: 'Let that blood be on Joab and his whole family! May his house always have somebody sick, broke, crippled, or dyin' by the sword.'
3.30: Joab and his brother Abishai did Abner like that 'cause he had killed their brother Asahel back at Gibeon.
3.31: David told Joab and all his men, 'Tear your clothes, throw on sackcloth, and mourn for Abner.' Then he followed behind the coffin.
3.32: They buried Abner in Hebron. David stood at the grave cryin', and everybody else wept too.
3.33: Then David sang a funeral song for Abner: 'Did Abner really have to go out like that?'
3.34: 'He wasn't bound up, he wasn't chained, yet he fell like somebody who got done dirty by thugs.'
3.35: Later, people tried to get David to eat while it was still daytime, but he swore, 'Man, may God deal with me if I eat before the sun goes down!'
3.36: The people saw this and respected David even more, 'cause he always did right by folks.
3.37: That day, everybody in Israel realized that David had nothin' to do with Abner's murder.
3.38: David told his people, 'Y'all see this? A real one just got taken out today in Israel.'
3.39: 'I may be king, but I feel powerless against these sons of Zeruiah—they reckless. The Most High gon' deal with them accordingly.'

4.1: When Saul's son, Ishbosheth, heard Abner got murked in Hebron, he straight-up lost his nerve. The whole nation of Israel was shook.
4.2: Now Ishbosheth had two dudes under him—military captains—Baanah and Rechab. They was sons of Rimmon, a Beerothite from the tribe of Benjamin.
4.3: Side note: The Beerothites had dipped to Gittaim a while back and been livin' there ever since.
4.4: Also, Saul's grandson, Mephibosheth—Jonathan's son—was crippled. When he was five, the news came that Saul and Jonathan was dead. His nurse tried to run with him, but she dropped him, and dude ended up lame for life.
4.5: So Rechab and Baanah pulled up at Ishbosheth's crib in the middle of the day, while he was laid up takin' a nap.
4.6: They rolled up inside like they was just there to grab some wheat, but instead, they stabbed him in the stomach. Then they took off.
4.7: After they got in his house, saw him laid up in bed, they straight-up killed him, chopped off his head, and dipped out, movin' all night across the plains.
4.8: They took Ishbosheth's head to David at Hebron, talkin' 'bout, 'Yo, King, look at this! This here is the head of Saul's son—the same dude who was tryna take you out. The Most High just avenged you today!'
4.9: But David looked at them and said, 'As The Most High lives—the one who got me through all my struggles—'
4.10: 'Let me remind y'all—when that other dude thought he was bringin' me good news about Saul dyin', thinkin' I was finna reward him, what happened? I had him executed on sight in Ziklag.'
4.11: 'So if I did that to him, what y'all think gon' happen to y'all? Y'all done killed a man in his own house, while he was laid up in bed. Y'all really thought I was finna celebrate this?'
4.12: David ain't waste no time. He told his men, 'Handle that.' And they did—Rechab and Baanah got executed on the spot. They even cut off their hands and feet, then hung 'em up by the pool in Hebron. But they took Ishbosheth's head and buried it in Abner's tomb in Hebron.

5.1: All the tribes of Israel pulled up to David at Hebron and said, 'Look, we family—we your flesh and blood.'
5.2: 'Even when Saul was king, you was the one leadin' us in battle. And The Most High already told you, "You gon' be the one to lead my people and rule over Israel."'
5.3: So all the elders of Israel came through to Hebron, and David made a covenant with them before The Most High. They anointed him king over all Israel.
5.4: David was 30 when he became king, and he reigned for 40 years.
5.5: He ruled Judah from Hebron for seven years and six months, then ruled all Israel and Judah from Jerusalem for thirty-three years.
5.6: David and his squad rolled up to Jerusalem to face the Jebusites—the folks livin' there. The Jebusites was talkin' trash, sayin', 'Man, you ain't gettin' in here. Even our blind and lame could hold you off!'
5.7: But David wasn't havin' it—he took over the stronghold of Zion, which became the City of David.
5.8: That day, David said, 'Whoever climbs up through the water tunnel and takes out these Jebusites—the so-called "lame and blind" that I can't stand—he gon' be the new commander.' That's why folks say, 'The blind and the lame can't come up in here.'
5.9: David moved into the stronghold and called it the City of David. Then he built up the area, starting from the Millo and working inward.
5.10: David kept rising up, and The Most High, the Lord of Heaven's Armies, was with him.
5.11: Hiram, king of Tyre, sent messengers to David, along with cedar wood, carpenters, and stonemasons. They built David a palace.
5.12: David realized that The Most High had established him as king over Israel and was lifting him up for the sake of His people.
5.13: David took more concubines and wives in Jerusalem after leavin' Hebron, and he had more sons and daughters.
5.14: These the names of his kids born in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
5.17: When the Philistines heard David got crowned king over Israel, they all went out lookin' for him. But David got word and dipped down to his stronghold.
5.18: The Philistines spread out across the Valley of Rephaim, tryna set up shop.
5.19: David checked in with The Most High, askin', 'Should I run up on these Philistines? You gon' put 'em in my hands?'
5.20: The Most High told him, 'Go ahead, I got you—you gon' take 'em down.' So David pulled up to Baal Perazim, wrecked 'em, and said, 'The Most High broke through my enemies like floodwaters!' That's why they called it Baal Perazim (which means 'Breakthrough Spot').
5.21: The Philistines ran off so quick, they left their idols behind. David and his crew scooped 'em up.
5.22: But them Philistines wasn't done. They regrouped and posted up in the Valley of Rephaim again.
5.23: David checked in with The Most High again, and this time, God said, 'Don't attack straight on. Go around behind 'em and hit 'em near the mulberry trees.'
5.24: 'When you hear the sound of soldiers marchin' on top of them trees, that's your cue—move fast, 'cause that's Me goin' ahead of you to take out the Philistine camp.'
5.25: David did exactly what The Most High said, and he pushed the Philistines all the way back from Geba to Gezer.

6.1: David rounded up 30,000 of Israel's top men and got 'em all together.
6.2: Then he and his squad rolled out from Baale Judah to go bring back the Ark of God—the one called by The Most High's Name, the Lord of Heaven's Armies, who stays between the cherubim.
6.3: They put the Ark of God on a brand-new cart and took it out of Abinadab's house on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio—Abinadab's sons—was drivin' that cart.
6.4: Ahio was up front, leadin' the way while they took the Ark out.
6.5: David and all of Israel was out there jammin'—playin' music for The Most High with harps, lyres, tambourines, rattles, and cymbals. Straight-up celebration mode.
6.6: But when they got to Nachon's threshing floor, the oxen tripped. Uzzah reached out to grab the Ark and keep it from fallin'.
6.7: That made The Most High furious. Uzzah got struck right then and there for disrespectin' the Ark. He dropped dead on the spot, right next to the Ark of God.
6.8: David was mad about it—real heated. He named that spot Perez Uzzah, and that's what it's still called.
6.9: But after that, David got shook. He was like, 'Man, how we supposed to bring this Ark to me?'
6.10: So instead of takin' it straight to the City of David, David sent it to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.
6.11: The Ark stayed at Obed-Edom's house for three months, and The Most High blessed him and his whole family for keepin' it.
6.12: Somebody told David, 'Yo, The Most High been blessin' Obed-Edom big time 'cause of the Ark!' So David was like, 'Bet!' and went to bring the Ark to the City of David—this time, with pure joy.
6.13: After they carried the Ark six steps, David stopped and offered up some sacrifices—oxen and fattened sheep.
6.14: Then David broke out dancin'—hard—before The Most High. Dude was gettin' it, wearin' his linen ephod.
6.15: David and all of Israel brought the Ark back with shouts and trumpet blasts—full-blown praise session.
6.16: As the Ark rolled into the City of David, Michal—Saul's daughter—was peepin' through the window. She saw David leaping and spinnin' like crazy before The Most High, and she started lookin' down on him.
6.17: They brought the Ark in and set it up in the tent David had made for it. Then David gave burnt offerings and peace offerings to The Most High.
6.18: Once David was done with all that, he blessed the people in The Most High's Name.
6.19: Then he gave out food to everybody—a loaf of bread, some meat, and a raisin cake to every man and woman. After that, folks went home.
6.20: When David got home to bless his own household, Michal came at him. She was like, 'Wow, look at the king of Israel today—out here embarrassin' himself in front of all the servant girls, actin' like some common street dude.'
6.21: David clapped back, 'I was dancin' for The Most High, the same one who chose me over your daddy and his whole family, makin' me ruler over Israel. So yeah, I'ma praise Him!'
6.22: 'Matter fact, I'ma go even harder than this next time. You might think I look foolish, but those same servant girls you talkin' about? They gon' respect me for it.'
6.23: And just like that, Michal—Saul's daughter—never had kids for the rest of her life.

7.1: So David was chillin' in his palace, finally at peace 'cause The Most High had shut down all his enemies.
7.2: Then he told the prophet Nathan, 'Look, I'm livin' in this fly crib made of cedar wood, but The Most High's Ark still sittin' in a tent.'
7.3: Nathan told him, 'Go 'head and do what's on your heart, 'cause The Most High is with you.'
7.4: But that same night, The Most High came to Nathan with a word.
7.5: 'Go tell my servant David: "So you think you gon' build a house for me to live in?"'
7.6: 'I been movin' from place to place since Egypt, stayin' in a tent this whole time.'
7.7: 'Did I ever tell any of the leaders I put in charge, 'Yo, why ain't y'all built me a cedar house yet?' Nope.'
7.8: 'So here's what you tell David: "I pulled you out the sheep fields, took you from watchin' flocks to rulin' Israel."'
7.9: 'I been with you everywhere you went, knocked down all your enemies, and made your name great—like the biggest names on Earth.'
7.10: 'I'ma set up a home for my people Israel, where they can stay without evil folks messin' with them like before.'
7.11: 'Since back when I put judges over Israel, I been givin' you peace from your enemies. But now, The Most High sayin' He gon' build YOU a house.'
7.12: 'When your time comes and you rest with your ancestors, I'ma raise up one of your own sons to take your place, and I'ma establish his kingdom.'
7.13: 'He gon' build a house for My name, and I'ma make sure his kingdom last forever.'
7.14: 'I'ma be his Father, and he gon' be my son. If he mess up, I'ma check him like a father do, with discipline from people.'
7.15: 'But I ain't never takin' my love away from him like I did Saul, the one I removed for you.'
7.16: 'Your house, your kingdom, and your throne gon' last forever in My sight.'
7.17: Nathan told David everything The Most High had said, straight up.
7.18: Then David went and sat before The Most High, sayin', 'Who am I, Lord? Who is my family, that You done brought me this far?'
7.19: 'And You tellin' me this is just the beginning? You plannin' all this for my future too?'
7.20: 'What else can I even say? You already know me inside and out.'
7.21: 'You did all this, not for me, but for Your word's sake—to make sure Your servant really understands.'
7.22: 'That's why You're so great, Lord! Ain't nobody like You. No other god can compare to what we been told about You.'
7.23: 'What other nation got a story like ours? You picked Israel as Your people, went and rescued us Yourself, and made a name for Yourself with all the wild, powerful things You did!'
7.24: 'You made Israel Your people forever, and You, Lord, became our God.'
7.25: 'So now, Lord, everything You promised about me and my family? Make it happen. Let it stand forever.'
7.26: 'Let Your name be lifted up forever, so folks will say, "The Lord Almighty is God over Israel!" Let my house stand strong before You.'
7.27: ''Cause You, Lord, told me You would build me a house. That's why I'm comin' to You with this prayer.'
7.28: 'Lord, You are God, and everything You say is true. And You promised this goodness to Your servant.'
7.29: 'So please, bless my house, let it stand forever before You. 'Cause when You bless somethin', Lord, it stays blessed forever.'

8.1: After all that, David ran up on the Philistines, put 'em in their place, and took Metheg Ammah from their hands.
8.2: Then he handled Moab—made them get down on the ground, lined 'em up, and measured 'em out. Two lines meant death, one line meant they could live. From that day on, Moab had to serve David and pay up.
8.3: David also went after Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah, 'cause he was tryna take back his land near the Euphrates River.
8.4: David took 1,000 chariots, 700 horsemen, and 20,000 foot soldiers from him. He hamstrung most of the chariot horses but kept enough for 100 chariots.
8.5: Then the Syrians from Damascus came through to help Hadadezer, but David wasn't havin' it—he killed 22,000 of them.
8.6: David set up military outposts in Syria, and the Syrians had to start paying tribute. No matter where David went, The Most High had his back.
8.7: He took all the golden shields from Hadadezer's crew and brought 'em back to Jerusalem.
8.8: He also took a whole lot of bronze from Betah and Berothai, cities that belonged to Hadadezer.
8.9: When Toi, king of Hamath, heard that David had wiped out Hadadezer's whole army, he saw the writing on the wall.
8.10: So Toi sent his son Joram to roll up on David with gifts—silver, gold, and bronze. He came through to bless David, 'cause Toi and Hadadezer had beef for a long time.
8.11: David didn't keep none of it for himself—he dedicated all the gold and silver to The Most High, just like he did with all the loot from the nations he conquered.
8.12: This included Syria, Moab, Ammon, the Philistines, Amalek, and the stuff he took from Hadadezer.
8.13: David got real famous after he came back from droppin' 18,000 Syrians in the Valley of Salt.
8.14: He also set up garrisons in Edom, puttin' his people everywhere. The Edomites had no choice but to serve David. The Most High kept him winnin' no matter what.
8.15: David ruled over all of Israel, makin' sure things was fair and just for everybody.
8.16: Joab, son of Zeruiah, was in charge of the army. Jehoshaphat, son of Ahilud, handled the records.
8.17: Zadok, son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech, son of Abiathar, were the priests. Seraiah was the scribe.
8.18: Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, ran the Cherethites and Pelethites (David's personal security). And David's own sons were top officials in his administration.

9.1: One day, David was like, 'Is there anybody left from Saul's family? I wanna show 'em some love for Jonathan's sake.'
9.2: They found a servant from Saul's house named Ziba and brought him to David. The king asked, 'You Ziba?' Ziba said, 'Yeah, that's me!'
9.3: Then David asked, 'Ain't nobody else left from Saul's family that I can bless the way The Most High would?' Ziba said, 'Well… there's one—Jonathan's son, Mephibosheth. But he crippled in both feet.'
9.4: David asked, 'Where he at?' Ziba said, 'He stayin' in Lo Debar, at the house of Machir, son of Ammiel.'
9.5: So David sent his people to go get Mephibosheth from Machir's house in Lo Debar.
9.6: When Mephibosheth, son of Jonathan (and grandson of Saul), showed up, he fell on his face in front of David. David said, 'Mephibosheth?' And he answered, 'Yes, I'm here, your humble servant.'
9.7: David told him, 'Aye, don't be scared. I got nothin' but love for you 'cause of your father Jonathan. I'ma give you back all your granddaddy Saul's land, and from now on, you gon' eat at my table like family.'
9.8: Mephibosheth bowed and said, 'Why you even lookin' out for me? I ain't nothin' but a dead dog to you.'
9.9: Then David called Ziba and said, 'Listen, I just gave Mephibosheth everything that used to belong to Saul and his family.'
9.10: 'So you, your sons, and your servants gon' work the land for him, bring in the crops, and make sure he got food. But Mephibosheth himself? He gon' eat at my table every day, just like one of my own sons.' (Ziba, by the way, had 15 sons and 20 servants.)
9.11: Ziba said, 'King, whatever you say—I'ma do it.' Then David repeated, 'Mephibosheth gon' eat at my table, same as my own sons.'
9.12: Now Mephibosheth had a son named Micha, and everybody in Ziba's house now worked for him.
9.13: Mephibosheth moved to Jerusalem, and from then on, he ate at the king's table every day. And yeah—he was still crippled in both feet.

10.1: Sometime later, the king of Ammon died, and his son Hanun took over.
10.2: David was like, 'I'ma show Hanun some love 'cause his pops, Nahash, looked out for me.' So David sent some of his men to send condolences about his father.
10.3: But the Ammonite princes got in Hanun's ear, sayin', 'You really think David sent his people to honor your father? Nah, bruh. He sent 'em to spy on us, check out the city, and plot against us.'
10.4: So Hanun humiliated them—shaved off half their beards, cut their robes at the waist (exposin' their behinds), and sent 'em off lookin' crazy.
10.5: When David heard about it, he sent word to his men, tellin' them, 'Stay in Jericho till y'all beards grow back, then come home.' 'Cause they was real embarrassed.
10.6: The Ammonites realized they had seriously messed up with David, so they hired some backup—20,000 Syrian foot soldiers from Beth Rehob & Zoba, plus 1,000 men from Maacah, and 12,000 from Ish-Tob.
10.7: When David got the news, he sent Joab and his elite troops out to handle business.
10.8: The Ammonites lined up outside their city gates, ready to fight, while their Syrian backup was posted out in the open field.
10.9: Joab saw they had enemies in front and behind, so he split the army. He took Israel's best soldiers to fight the Syrians.
10.10: Then he put the rest under his brother Abishai, so they could hold it down against the Ammonites.
10.11: Joab told Abishai, 'Aye, if the Syrians come too hard, you got my back. And if the Ammonites get the upper hand on you, I got you.'
10.12: 'Stay strong, fam. Let's fight for our people and for God's cities. And whatever happens, The Most High gon' do what He do.'
10.13: Joab and his soldiers charged the Syrians, and the Syrians straight ran for their lives.
10.14: When the Ammonites saw their backup running scared, they took off too—ran back inside their city. So Joab and his crew left and went back to Jerusalem.
10.15: But the Syrians ain't take the L lightly. They regrouped for round two.
10.16: Hadadezer called in reinforcements from beyond the Euphrates River, and his commander Shobach led the army to a place called Helam.
10.17: David heard what was goin' down, so he gathered all of Israel, crossed the Jordan River, and met the Syrians head-on at Helam.
10.18: The Syrians lost bad—they tried to run, but David's army caught 'em. David killed 700 charioteers and 40,000 horsemen, plus took out their top general, Shobach, right there on the battlefield.
10.19: When the other kings under Hadadezer saw they ain't stand a chance, they made peace with David and started servin' him. From then on, the Syrians were too scared to help the Ammonites ever again.

11.1: It was springtime—the season when kings usually went out to battle. David sent Joab, his servants, and all of Israel to handle the Ammonites and siege Rabbah, but David stayed back in Jerusalem.
11.2: One evening, David got up from his bed, walked around on the rooftop of his palace, and spotted a woman bathing. She was fine as can be.
11.3: David got curious and asked about her. Somebody told him, 'That's Bathsheba, daughter of Eliam—Uriah the Hittite's wife.'
11.4: But David sent for her anyway. She came through, and he slept with her. After that, she went back home.
11.5: A little while later, she sent word to David: 'I'm pregnant.'
11.6: So David hit up Joab: 'Send Uriah the Hittite to me.' Joab sent him over.
11.7: When Uriah arrived, David played it cool—asked him how Joab was doin', how the battle was goin'.
11.8: Then David told Uriah, 'Go home, clean up, relax.' David even sent a gift to his house after him.
11.9: But Uriah didn't go home. Instead, he slept outside with the palace guards.
11.10: David got the report: 'Uriah ain't go home.' So he asked, 'Bruh, you just came from the battlefield. Why didn't you go home?'
11.11: Uriah said, 'The Ark, Israel, and Judah are all in tents. Joab and the soldiers are in the field fightin'—how I'ma go home, eat, drink, and be with my wife? I ain't doin' it, King, not while my brothers at war.'
11.12: David told him, 'Stay here another day, then I'll send you back.' So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem.
11.13: That night, David invited him to dinner and got him drunk. But even after that, Uriah still didn't go home—he slept outside with the guards again.
11.14: By morning, David had enough. He wrote a letter to Joab and had Uriah deliver his own death sentence.
11.15: The letter said: 'Put Uriah on the front lines where the battle is the worst, then pull back so he gets killed.'
11.16: Joab followed orders—he put Uriah in the heat of the battle, right where the toughest warriors were.
11.17: And just like that, the enemy came out strong, some of David's men got killed, and Uriah the Hittite died, too.
11.18: Joab sent a messenger to report the battle news back to David.
11.19: He told the messenger, 'After you tell the king everything, if he gets mad about us fightin' too close to the city walls…'
11.20: And if he brings up how Abimelech got killed by a woman who dropped a millstone on him in Thebez, just tell him: "Uriah the Hittite is dead, too."
11.21: The messenger went to David and gave him the full report.
11.22: He said, 'The enemy came out strong, we pushed them back to the city gate…'
11.23: But they hit us with arrows from the walls. Some of your soldiers died, and… Uriah the Hittite is dead, too.'
11.24: David told the messenger, 'Tell Joab not to stress. War takes people out—one way or another. Keep pushin' against the city and take it down.' Then he told the messenger to hype Joab up.
11.25: When Bathsheba heard her husband Uriah was dead, she mourned for him.
11.26: After her mourning period was over, David sent for her, brought her to the palace, married her, and she had a son.
11.27: But The Most High was NOT pleased with what David had done.

12.1: The Most High sent Nathan to David. Nathan pulled up and told him a story: 'There were two men in a city—one was rich, the other was poor.'
12.2: 'The rich man had plenty—flocks and herds for days.'
12.3: 'The poor man? He only had one little lamb that he raised with love. The lamb ate from his plate, drank from his cup, and even slept in his arms—like a daughter to him.'
12.4: 'Then one day, a traveler came to visit the rich man. But instead of using his own sheep, he took the poor man's lamb, killed it, and served it up for dinner.'
12.5: David got heated when he heard this. He said, 'Whoever did this deserves to DIE!'
12.6: 'And on top of that, he gotta pay back four times what he took, 'cause he had no mercy!'
12.7: Nathan looked at David and said, 'YOU that man. The Most High says: "I made you king over Israel, saved you from Saul's hands,"
12.8: 'I gave you power, wealth, and wives, and if that wasn't enough, I would've given you more.'
12.9: 'But you disrespected My commands, took Uriah's wife, and had him killed in battle.'
12.10: 'So from now on, your family gon' deal with the sword nonstop, 'cause you disrespected Me and took Uriah's wife.'
12.11: 'And guess what? Trouble gon' rise from your own house. I'ma take your wives and give 'em to another man, and he gon' sleep with 'em out in the open.'
12.12: 'You did your dirt in secret, but I'ma expose you in front of everybody!'
12.13: David finally broke down: 'I messed up. I sinned against The Most High.'
12.14: Nathan said, 'The Most High already put your sin away—you won't die. But since you did this, and folks gon' use it to slander The Most High, your child will die.'
12.15: Then Nathan left, and soon after, The Most High struck Bathsheba's child with sickness.
12.16: David begged The Most High for the child's life. He fasted, laid on the ground all night, prayin'.
12.17: His people tried to get him up, but he wouldn't move—wouldn't even eat.
12.18: On the seventh day, the child died. But David's servants were scared to tell him, thinkin' he might hurt himself.
12.19: But David peeped the whispers and asked, 'The child gone, ain't he?' They answered, 'Yeah, he gone.'
12.20: So David got up, washed up, put on fresh clothes, went to The Most High's house, worshiped, then went home and asked for food.
12.21: His servants were confused: 'When the child was sick, you wouldn't eat, but now that he's dead, you eatin'?'
12.22: David said, 'While he was alive, I prayed and fasted, hopin' The Most High might show mercy.'
12.23: 'But now that he's gone, why fast? I can't bring him back. One day, I'ma go where he is, but he ain't comin' back to me.'
12.24: Later, David comforted Bathsheba, they slept together, and she had another son—Solomon.
12.25: The Most High loved Solomon, so He sent Nathan to name him Jedidiah (which means "loved by The Most High").
12.26: Meanwhile, Joab was fightin' in Rabbah against the Ammonites and had taken the royal city.
12.27: He sent word to David, sayin', 'I took over their water supply.'
12.28: 'Bring the rest of the army, take the city, or they might start callin' it my city instead of yours.'
12.29: So David gathered his forces, pulled up on Rabbah, and took it.
12.30: He took the king's crown, which weighed about 75 pounds of gold and had precious stones in it, and put it on his own head. Then he looted the city big time.
12.31: He put the Ammonite people to work with saws, iron picks, and axes, makin' them work in brick factories. He did this to all the Ammonite cities. Then David and his crew went back to Jerusalem.

13.1: David's son Absalom had a beautiful sister named Tamar, and his half-brother Amnon was obsessed with her.
13.2: Amnon was so pressed that he made himself sick over Tamar, 'cause she was a virgin and it wasn't right for him to mess with her.
13.3: But Amnon had a slick cousin named Jonadab, son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab was real sneaky.
13.4: Jonadab asked him, 'Bruh, you the king's son, why you lookin' so down every day? What's up?'
13.5: Amnon told him, 'I'm in love with Tamar—Absalom's sister.'
13.6: Jonadab gave him a dirty plan: 'Act like you sick, lay in bed, and when your dad comes, tell him to send Tamar to cook for you.'
13.7: So David sent for Tamar, tellin' her, 'Go to Amnon's house and fix him some food.'
13.8: Tamar went to Amnon's crib, where he was laid up. She made the food in front of him and baked the cakes.
13.9: But when she brought the food, Amnon refused to eat. He told everyone, 'Get out.' They all left.
13.10: Then Amnon told Tamar, 'Bring the food to my bedroom, I wanna eat from your hand.'
13.11: As soon as she got close, he grabbed her and said, "Come sleep with me, sis."
13.12: Tamar was like, 'No, my brother! This is wrong—this kinda stuff shouldn't happen in Israel!'
13.13: 'Where would I go with this shame? And you—you'd be just another fool! Please, just ask the king, he won't hold me back from you!'
13.14: But Amnon didn't listen. He was stronger than her, so he forced himself on her.
13.15: Then, outta nowhere, he started hatin' her—hated her more than he ever claimed to love her. He told her, 'Get up and get out.'
13.16: Tamar begged him, 'Sending me away is worse than what you already did!'
13.17: But Amnon didn't care. He called his servant and said, 'Throw this woman out and lock the door.'
13.18: Tamar was wearing a royal robe, like all the king's virgin daughters. But the servant put her out and locked the door behind her.
13.19: Tamar put ashes on her head, ripped her robe, put her hands on her head, and walked away crying her heart out.
13.20: Absalom saw her and said, 'Did Amnon do this to you? Look, sis, don't say anything right now. Just stay here with me.'
13.21: When King David heard what happened, he was furious.
13.22: But Absalom never said a word to Amnon—good or bad. But deep down, he hated him for what he did to Tamar.
13.23: Two years later, Absalom threw a big feast for the sheepshearers near Ephraim. He invited all the king's sons.
13.24: Absalom told his father, 'Come celebrate with us! You and all your servants.'
13.25: David was like, 'Nah, if we all go, it'll be too much. But thanks for the invite, son.'
13.26: Then Absalom said, 'Well, at least let Amnon come.'
13.27: David was suspicious, 'Why you want Amnon to go?' But Absalom kept askin', so he finally let all his sons go, including Amnon.
13.28: Absalom had already planned it. He told his servants, 'Wait 'til Amnon gets drunk, then when I say the word—kill him. Don't be scared, just do what I say!'
13.29: So as soon as Amnon was lit, Absalom's servants killed him on the spot. The rest of the king's sons jumped on their mules and got outta there.
13.30: As they were ridin' back, David got fake news: 'Absalom killed all your sons—none of them made it!'
13.31: David tore his clothes and fell to the ground in grief. His servants did the same.
13.32: But Jonadab, the sneaky cousin, told David, 'Nah, it ain't all your sons—just Amnon. Absalom been plottin' this since the day Amnon violated Tamar.'
13.34: Meanwhile, Absalom fled. And as he ran, a lookout saw a group of men coming down the road.
13.35: Jonadab told the king, 'See? Your sons are alive, just like I said.'
13.36: As soon as they arrived, they broke down crying. David and his servants cried even harder.
13.37: But Absalom escaped to Geshur, to his grandfather Talmai, king of Geshur. And David mourned for Amnon every day.
13.38: Absalom stayed in Geshur for three years.
13.39: David missed Absalom but had made peace with Amnon being gone.

14.1: Joab, son of Zeruiah, peeped that David was still thinking about Absalom.
14.2: So Joab went to Tekoa, found a wise woman, and told her, 'Act like you been mourning for a long time. Put on your sad clothes, don't wear no oil, and go talk to the king.'
14.3: 'Tell him this story I'ma give you.' And Joab coached her on what to say.
14.4: The woman went to David, fell on her face, and cried out, 'Help me, O king!'
14.5: David asked, 'What's wrong?' She said, 'I'm a widow. My husband is gone.'
14.6: 'I had two sons—they got into it in the field, nobody was there to break it up, and one killed the other.'
14.7: 'Now the whole family wanna execute my only son, sayin' he gotta pay for his brother's death. If they do that, they wipin' out my husband's legacy completely.'
14.8: David told her, 'Go home, I'ma handle it.'
14.9: But the woman said, 'If anybody got a problem, let the blame be on me and my family—not you.'
14.10: David reassured her, 'If anybody says somethin', bring 'em to me—I won't let them touch you.'
14.11: She pushed further, 'Swear to The Most High that you won't let the avenger of blood come for my son.'
14.12: David swore, 'As The Most High lives, not one hair on your son's head will fall.'
14.13: Then she hit David with the real message: 'So why you treatin' your own banished son like this? You just ruled in my favor, but you won't bring Absalom home?'
14.14: 'We all gonna die one day, like spilled water you can't scoop back up. But The Most High finds a way to bring folks back, instead of throwin' 'em away.'
14.15: 'That's why I came to you today—I was scared, hopin' the king would hear me out.'
14.16: 'I know the king got wisdom from The Most High, so I trust you gon' do what's right.'
14.17: 'Your servant believes that my lord the king gon' make the right call—'cause you got wisdom like an angel of God, always knowin' what's good and what's bad. May The Most High be with you!'
14.18: David looked at her and said, 'Tell me the truth—did Joab put you up to this?'
14.19: She smiled and said, 'You got me, king. Joab told me what to say, but you saw right through it.'
14.20: 'He did it to get you to see the bigger picture. But you wise, king—you always know what's goin' on.'
14.21: David sighed and told Joab, 'Alright, go bring Absalom back.'
14.22: Joab bowed down, thanked David, and said, 'I know now that I got favor with you, king.'
14.23: So Joab went to Geshur and brought Absalom back to Jerusalem.
14.24: But David said, 'He can come back, but he ain't gonna see my face.' So Absalom stayed in his house and didn't see the king.
14.25: Absalom was the finest dude in Israel—from head to toe, not a flaw on him.
14.26: His hair was legendary—dude only cut it once a year 'cause it got too heavy. When he did, it weighed about five pounds!
14.27: Absalom had three sons and a daughter named Tamar, who was beautiful just like her aunt.
14.28: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years but still hadn't seen David.
14.29: He sent for Joab to talk to the king, but Joab ignored him. He sent for him again, and Joab still didn't come.
14.30: So Absalom told his servants, 'Joab's field is next to mine, right? He got some barley? Go burn it down.'
14.31: Joab finally pulled up, mad as ever: 'Bruh, why you burnin' my field?!'
14.32: Absalom said, 'Cause I told you to come and you ignored me! Why'd I even leave Geshur if my father ain't gon' see me? If I did something wrong, let him kill me.'
14.33: So Joab told the king what Absalom said. David finally called for Absalom. Absalom came in, bowed before the king, and David kissed him.

15.1: After a while, Absalom started flexin'—he got himself chariots, horses, and fifty men runnin' ahead of him.
15.2: Every morning, he'd post up near the city gate, waitin' for folks comin' to see the king about legal matters.
15.3: When people pulled up, he'd be like, 'Where you from?' They'd tell him their tribe, and Absalom would say, 'Man, you got a solid case, but too bad the king ain't got nobody to hear you.'
15.4: Then he'd hit 'em with, "If I was judge, I'd make sure everybody got justice!"
15.5: Anytime someone came to bow to him, he'd grab 'em and hug 'em like family.
15.6: Little by little, he stole the hearts of the people—gettin' them on his side instead of David's.
15.7: After four years, Absalom told David, 'Let me go to Hebron and fulfill a vow I made to The Most High.'
15.8: 'Back when I was in Geshur, I promised that if The Most High brought me back to Jerusalem, I'd serve Him.'
15.9: David told him, 'Alright, go in peace.' So Absalom left for Hebron.
15.10: But this was all a setup. Absalom sent spies to all the tribes of Israel, tellin' them, 'When you hear the trumpet blow, tell everybody, "Absalom is king in Hebron!"'
15.11: He took 200 men from Jerusalem with him, but they didn't know what was goin' on.
15.12: Then he called Ahithophel, David's top adviser, to join him. The conspiracy kept growing, and more people started backin' Absalom.
15.13: A messenger ran to David, sayin', 'The people ridin' with Absalom now!'
15.14: David told his men, 'We gotta GO! If we stay here, we won't make it. Absalom finna roll up on us quick, and he gon' wipe out the whole city.'
15.15: David's servants told him, 'Whatever you say, King—we wit' you.'
15.16: David and his whole household left, but he left ten of his concubines behind to take care of the palace.
15.17: They stopped at the last house before leavin' the city,
15.18: David's whole squad marched past him—the Cherethites, Pelethites, and 600 Gittites from Gath.
15.19: David looked at Ittai the Gittite and said, 'Bruh, you a foreigner. Why you ridin' with me? Go back to Absalom.'
15.20: 'You just got here yesterday—no need to get caught up in this. Go back and be safe.'
15.21: Ittai said, 'Nah, King. Wherever you go, I go—life or death.'
15.22: David nodded and said, 'Alright, come on then.' So Ittai, his men, and their families crossed the Kidron Valley.
15.23: Everybody was cryin' as David and his people crossed over, headin' toward the wilderness.
15.24: Zadok the priest and the Levites brought the Ark of God, but David told 'em, 'Take it back to the city.'
15.25: 'If The Most High wants me back, He'll bring me back. If not, let His will be done.'
15.26: Then he told Zadok, 'Stay in the city and keep watch. If anything pops off, send word through your sons, Ahimaaz and Jonathan.'
15.27: So Zadok and Abiathar took the Ark back to Jerusalem.
15.28: David and his people kept movin' into the wilderness.
15.29: So Zadok and Abiathar did what David said—they took the Ark of God back to Jerusalem and stayed put.
15.30: David climbed the Mount of Olives, cryin', barefoot, and with his head covered. Everybody with him did the same.
15.31: Then he got bad news: "Ahithophel is ridin' with Absalom." David prayed, 'Lord, turn Ahithophel's advice into nonsense!'
15.32: At the top of the mountain, David saw Hushai the Archite, his robe torn, dust on his head—he was mournin' too.
15.33: David told him, 'If you come with me, you just gon' slow us down.'
15.34: 'But if you go back to Absalom and act like you his servant, you can mess up Ahithophel's advice for me.'
15.35: Zadok and Abiathar the priests gon' be there too—whatever you hear, tell them.
15.36: Then they'll send word to me through their sons, Ahimaaz and Jonathan.
15.37: So Hushai went back to Jerusalem, just as Absalom rolled into the city.

16.1: As David got past the top of the mountain, Ziba, Mephibosheth's servant, pulled up with two saddled donkeys loaded with 200 loaves of bread, 100 clusters of raisins, 100 summer fruits, and a skin of wine.
16.3: Ziba said, 'The donkeys for your people to ride, the food for your soldiers, and the wine for anybody who gets weak in the wilderness.'
16.5: Ziba lied and said, 'He stayed in Jerusalem talkin' 'bout "Today, Israel gon' give me back my granddaddy Saul's kingdom."'
16.6: David told Ziba, 'Aight, everything that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours.'
16.7: Ziba bowed low and said, 'Thank you, my king!'
16.8: When David got to Bahurim, a man from Saul's family, Shimei son of Gera, came out cursin' him non-stop.
16.9: Dude was throwin' rocks at David and his men, even though David's soldiers surrounded him.
16.10: Shimei yelled, 'Get outta here, you murderer! You dirty man!'
16.11: 'The Most High is gettin' you back for all the blood you spilled in Saul's house! You took his throne, and now your own son is takin' yours. You gettin' what you deserve!'
16.12: Abishai, Joab's brother, got mad and told David, 'Why this dead dog talkin' to you like this? Let me go take his head off.'
16.13: But David said, 'Nah, let him talk. If The Most High let him curse me, who am I to stop him?'
16.14: 'My own son tryna kill me—this man just talkin'. Maybe The Most High seein' my pain and gon' bless me for this instead.'
16.15: Shimei kept cursin', throwin' rocks, and kickin' up dust as David walked by.
16.16: David and his people got tired and finally stopped to rest.
16.17: Meanwhile, Absalom rolled up in Jerusalem with his squad, and Ahithophel was with him.
16.18: Then Hushai, David's friend, pulled up to Absalom and said, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"
16.19: Absalom side-eyed him and said, 'So this how you do your boy David? Ain't you supposed to be ridin' with him?'
16.20: Hushai played along and said, 'Nah, I roll with whoever The Most High and Israel chooses. If that's you, then I'm wit' you.'
16.21: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, "What's the move? What should we do?"
16.22: Ahithophel told him, "Go sleep with your father's concubines—the ones he left behind to watch the palace. If you do that, all of Israel will know you and your father ain't never gon' make up. Then everybody that follows you will be even more solid."
16.23: So they set up a tent on the palace roof, and Absalom went in and slept with David's concubines—out in the open, for all of Israel to see.
16.24: Everybody listened to Ahithophel like his advice came straight from God. Both David and Absalom had relied on his counsel.

17.1: Ahithophel told Absalom, 'Let me pick 12,000 men and chase after David tonight.'
17.2: 'We gon' catch him while he's tired and weak, put fear in him, and make his people scatter. Then I'ma kill only the king.'
17.3: 'After that, everybody else gon' come back to you, and this whole thing will be over.'
17.4: Absalom and his advisors liked the plan—it sounded solid.
17.5: But Absalom said, 'Call Hushai, too—I wanna hear what he think.'
17.6: When Hushai came, Absalom told him, 'Ahithophel say we should attack David now. You agree, or you got a better idea?'
17.7: Hushai said, 'Nah, Ahithophel wrong on this one.'
17.8: 'You know your father and his men—they warriors. Right now, they mad as a mama bear that lost her cubs.'
17.9: 'David ain't stupid. He already hidin' somewhere—he ain't sittin' out in the open.'
17.10: 'And if your first attack don't go right, people gon' panic and say, "David's men are slaughterin' Absalom's troops!"'
17.11: 'So here's my advice—get ALL of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba—an army so big it look like sand on the beach. Then you lead the charge yourself.'
17.12: 'Wherever David tryna hide, we gon' flood him like morning dew, and won't leave a single one of them alive.'
17.13: 'And if he in a city, we gon' drag that whole city into the river 'til not even a stone is left.'
17.14: Absalom and his men chose Hushai's advice over Ahithophel's—'cause The Most High had already planned to mess up Ahithophel's wisdom to bring Absalom down.
17.15: Hushai ran to Zadok and Abiathar the priests and told them everything—both Ahithophel's plan and his own advice.
17.16: 'Y'all gotta send word to David fast—tell him to cross the river tonight, or he and his men are done for!'
17.17: Jonathan and Ahimaaz were at En Rogel, hidin', waitin' on a message. A servant girl came and passed them the word so they wouldn't get caught.
17.18: But somebody saw them and snitched to Absalom! So they took off and hid at a man's house in Bahurim—they jumped in a well in his courtyard.
17.19: His wife covered the well with cloth and spread grain over it, makin' it look normal.
17.20: Absalom's men showed up and asked, "Where's Jonathan and Ahimaaz?"
17.21: The woman played it smooth and said, "They already left—crossed the river."
17.22: As soon as Absalom's men left, Jonathan and Ahimaaz crawled out the well, ran to David, and told him, "You gotta cross the river NOW—Ahithophel wants you dead."
17.23: David and his whole crew crossed the Jordan by sunrise—nobody got left behind.
17.24: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom ignored his advice, he knew it was over for him.
17.25: He went home, put his affairs in order, then hung himself. They buried him in his father's tomb.
17.26: David made it to Mahanaim, while Absalom and his army crossed the Jordan and set up camp in Gilead.
17.27: Absalom replaced Joab with Amasa as commander of the army.
17.28: Meanwhile, David's people started getting supplies. Shobi from Ammon, Machir from Lo Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite pulled up with beds, pots, wheat, barley, beans, lentils, honey, sheep, and cheese.
17.29: They told David, "We know y'all tired, hungry, and thirsty out here in the wilderness—eat up."

18.1: David took count of his people, set up commanders over thousands and hundreds, gettin' them organized.
18.2: He split them into three groups—one under Joab, one under Abishai (Joab's brother), and one under Ittai the Gittite. David said, 'I'ma go out there with y'all.'
18.3: But the soldiers said, "Nah, King. You too important. If we run, they won't care. Even if half of us die, they still won't care. But you worth 10,000 of us. It's better if you stay back and help from the city."
18.4: David agreed and stood at the gate while his people marched out in groups.
18.5: Before they left, David told Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, "Look, deal gently with my son Absalom, for my sake." Everybody heard him say it.
18.6: The battle went down in the forest of Ephraim.
18.7: David's army crushed Absalom's men, takin' out 20,000 soldiers.
18.8: The battle was everywhere, and the forest itself took out more men than the sword did!
18.9: Then Absalom ran into David's soldiers. He was ridin' a mule, and as he passed under a big oak tree, his hair got caught in the branches!
18.10: His mule kept runnin', but he was stuck there, dangling between heaven and earth.
18.11: One of David's men saw it and ran to tell Joab.
18.12: Joab was like, 'You saw him and didn't kill him?! I would've given you ten pieces of silver and a belt!'
18.13: The man said, 'Man, even if you gave me a thousand silver pieces, I wouldn't touch the king's son. We all heard what the king said—nobody lay a hand on Absalom.'
18.14: Joab said, "I ain't got time for this." Then he grabbed three spears and drove them straight into Absalom's heart while he was still hangin' there alive.
18.15: Then ten of Joab's young men came through and finished Absalom off.
18.16: Joab blew the trumpet, tellin' David's army to stop chasin' Israel.
18.17: They threw Absalom's body in a big pit in the forest and stacked up a huge pile of stones over him. Everybody else ran back home.
18.18: Absalom had built a monument for himself in the King's Valley, 'cause he ain't have a son to carry on his name. That spot still called Absalom's Monument today.
18.19: Ahimaaz, son of Zadok, told Joab, "Let me run and tell the king the good news—The Most High gave him victory today!"
18.20: Joab said, "Nah, not today. The king's son is dead—you don't wanna be the one to tell him that."
18.21: Then he told a Cushite servant, "You go tell him." The Cushite bowed and ran.
18.22: Ahimaaz still wanted to go, so he begged Joab, "Please, let me run too!"
18.23: Joab was like, "Why? You got no good news." But Ahimaaz insisted, so Joab finally said, "Fine, go ahead." Ahimaaz ran the long way but still outran the Cushite!
18.24: David was sittin' at the city gate. His watchman climbed up, saw a man runnin' alone, and shouted down to the king.
18.25: David said, "If he runnin' solo, he bringin' news."
18.26: Then the watchman saw another man runnin' and told David.
18.27: The watchman was like, "That first runner look like Ahimaaz!"
18.28: Ahimaaz got there first, bowed before David, and said, "King, The Most High gave you victory today!"
18.29: David cut straight to the chase: "Is my son Absalom okay?"
18.30: Ahimaaz dodged the question: "I saw a big commotion, but I don't know what happened."
18.31: Then the Cushite came and told David, "Good news, King! The Most High got rid of your enemies today!"
18.32: David asked again, "But what about my son Absalom? Is he safe?"
18.33: The Cushite said, "May all your enemies end up like him."
18.34: David was crushed. He went up to his room cryin' and sayin', "My son, Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you! My son, my son!"

19.1: Somebody told Joab, 'The king still cryin' over Absalom.'
19.2: What should've been a day of victory turned into a sad day 'cause everybody heard that David was grieving his son.
19.3: Instead of celebratin', David's people snuck back into the city like they was ashamed, like they just lost a battle.
19.4: Meanwhile, David had his face covered, cryin' loud, 'My son Absalom! My son, my son!'
19.5: Joab stormed in and told David, 'Man, you trippin'! You out here disrespectin' the same people who just saved your life, your family, and your kingdom.'
19.6: 'It's like you love your enemies and hate your own people! You makin' it real clear—if Absalom was still alive and all of us was dead, that woulda made you happy!'
19.7: 'Now get up, go out there, and speak to your people! If you don't, I swear ain't nobody gonna be left by tomorrow! And trust me, that would be worse than any L you ever took.'
19.8: So David wiped his face, got up, and sat by the gate. When the people heard, they came through to see him.
19.9: All over Israel, people was arguin'— 'David saved us from the Philistines and all our enemies, but he ran when Absalom came for him.'
19.10: 'Now Absalom dead, but nobody sayin' nothin' about bringin' David back?'
19.11: David sent word to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, tellin' them to holler at the elders of Judah: 'Why y'all the last ones to invite me back when all Israel already want me home?'
19.12: 'Y'all my own flesh and blood! Why y'all movin' slow on this?'
19.13: David told them to tell Amasa (the guy Absalom put in charge), 'You family too! May God deal with me if I don't make you commander over the army instead of Joab.'
19.14: That move got Judah's heart back on David's side, and they sent him a message: 'Come back, King!'
19.15: So David started headin' back to Jerusalem, and the tribe of Judah met him at Gilgal to escort him across the Jordan.
19.16: Shimei (the dude that cursed David out last time) rushed down to meet him with 1,000 Benjamites.
19.17: Ziba (Saul's servant) showed up too, bringin' his 15 sons and 20 servants.
19.18: They hurried across the river to help the king's household cross.
19.19: Shimei fell on his face in front of David and said, 'King, please don't hold my past against me!'
19.20: 'I know I messed up, but I'm the first one here to welcome you back!'
19.21: Abishai wasn't feelin' it: 'Shouldn't Shimei be put to death? He cursed the Lord's anointed!'
19.22: But David shut that down: 'Man, what am I gon' do with y'all, Zeruiah's sons? Today ain't a day for killin'—I'm back as king!'
19.23: Then David told Shimei, 'You ain't gon' die.' And he made an oath on it.
19.24: Mephibosheth, Saul's grandson, finally showed up. He looked rough—hadn't taken care of his feet, beard, or clothes since David left.
19.25: David asked, 'Why you ain't come with me, Mephibosheth?'
19.26: Mephibosheth said, 'King, my servant lied on me! I told him to saddle up my donkey so I could ride with you, but he left me behind 'cause I'm crippled.
19.27: 'Then he went and lied to you about me, but you like an angel of God, so do whatever you think is right.'
19.28: 'My whole family was as good as dead, but you let me eat at your table. I ain't got the right to ask for nothin' more.'
19.29: David cut him off: 'Enough talk. You and Ziba split the land.'
19.30: But Mephibosheth said, 'Let him have it all. I'm just happy you home, King.'
19.31: Barzillai the Gileadite came through, escortin' David across the river.
19.32: Dude was 80 years old and had taken care of David while he was on the run.
19.33: David told him, 'Come to Jerusalem with me, I'll take care of you.'
19.34: But Barzillai said, 'Man, I'm old. What I'ma do in Jerusalem?'
19.35: 'I can't taste food right, I can't hear music, I don't need nothin' extra. Why burden you?'
19.36: 'I'll go with you just a little, but then let me go back home. I wanna die in my own city, near my parents' grave.'
19.37: 'But take Chimham instead—let him serve you. Do for him whatever you see fit.'
19.38: David agreed: 'Alright, Chimham can roll with me. I'll look out for him just like you asked.'
19.39: Then David crossed over, kissed Barzillai, blessed him, and Barzillai went back home.
19.40: David went on to Gilgal with Chimham. Judah escorted him, but only half of Israel showed up.
19.41: Then the Israelites came at David, mad: 'Why Judah bring you back without us? We part of Israel too!'
19.42: Judah clapped back: 'King David is family! Why y'all mad? We ain't get no gifts from him!'
19.43: Then Israel fired back: 'We got ten shares in the kingdom—we got more claim to David than y'all! But y'all ignored us and brought him back without askin' us first!'
19.44: The argument got heated—Judah's men spoke even fiercer than Israel's.

20.1: A troublemaker named Sheba, son of Bichri, a Benjamite, stood up and blew his trumpet, sayin': 'Forget David! We ain't got no part in Jesse's son. Every man, back to your tents, Israel!'
20.2: All of Israel dipped and followed Sheba, but the men of Judah stayed loyal to David.
20.3: When David got back to Jerusalem, he took his ten concubines, put them in seclusion, and took care of them, but he never slept with them again. They lived like widows for the rest of their lives.
20.4: David told Amasa, 'Round up Judah's army in three days and report back.'
20.5: But Amasa was takin' too long, so David told Abishai, 'Sheba might be a bigger problem than Absalom. Take my best men and stop him before he hides in a fortified city.
20.6: Joab's men, the Cherethites, Pelethites, and David's warriors rolled out to track Sheba down.
20.7: At Gibeon, Amasa finally showed up. Joab, dressed in his battle gear, stepped forward.
20.8: Joab walked up to Amasa like, 'How you doin', bro?' Then grabbed his beard like he was about to kiss him.
20.9: But Amasa ain't see the dagger in Joab's other hand—Joab stabbed him in the stomach, and his guts spilled out.
20.10: One of Joab's men shouted, 'If you ridin' with Joab and King David, let's go!'
20.11: But Amasa's body was just lyin' there, and people kept stoppin' when they saw it.
20.12: So they dragged him to the side of the road and threw a cloth over him. After that, everybody followed Joab to chase down Sheba.
20.13: Sheba traveled through all the tribes, then ended up in Abel of Beth Maachah.
20.14: Joab's army caught up and surrounded the city, buildin' a siege mound against the walls.
20.15: Then a wise woman inside the city called out, 'Somebody get Joab! I need to talk to him.'
20.16: Joab stepped up, and she asked, 'You Joab?' He said, 'Yeah, that's me.'
20.17: She told him, 'Look, our city got a reputation for bein' peaceful and wise.
20.18: 'We ain't tryin' to fight, but you about to destroy us—God's own people. Why?'
20.19: Joab said, 'Nah, I ain't tryna destroy y'all.
20.20: 'We just want one man—Sheba, son of Bichri. He rebelled against King David. Give him up, and we out.'
20.21: The woman went to the city leaders, they grabbed Sheba, cut off his head, and tossed it over the wall to Joab.
20.22: Joab blew his trumpet, called off the siege, and his men went back home.
20.23: Joab was back as commander of Israel's army.
20.24: Benaiah ran the Cherethites and Pelethites.
20.25: Adoram was in charge of taxes.
20.28: Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
20.29: Ira the Jairite was David's chief minister.

21.1: A famine hit the land for three straight years, so David asked The Most High what was up. The Lord said, 'It's 'cause of Saul and his bloodstained house—he tried to wipe out the Gibeonites.'
21.2: David called up the Gibeonites to make things right. They weren't Israelites but leftovers from the Amorites, and back in the day, Israel had promised to protect them. But Saul had broken that promise, tryna wipe them out to look good for Israel and Judah.
21.3: David asked them, 'What can I do to fix this? How can I make peace so The Most High blesses the land again?'
21.4: The Gibeonites told him, 'We don't want no silver or gold from Saul's house, and we ain't askin' for anybody in Israel to be killed.'
21.5: But they did want justice. 'Saul tried to wipe us out, so we want seven of his descendants. We'll execute them in Gibeah, Saul's hometown.'
21.7: But he spared Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, 'cause of the promise he made to Jonathan.
21.8: Instead, he took two sons of Rizpah (Saul's concubine) and five sons of Michal (Saul's daughter) and handed them over.
21.9: The Gibeonites executed them, hangin' them on a hill before The Most High. They were all killed at the beginning of the barley harvest.
21.10: Rizpah, heartbroken, spread out sackcloth on a rock and guarded the bodies, keepin' birds from touchin' them by day and wild animals away at night.
21.11: When David heard about Rizpah's devotion, he was moved.
21.12: He went and got the bones of Saul and Jonathan from Jabesh Gilead—where the Philistines had left them hangin' after they killed Saul in battle.
21.13: Then David gathered up the bones of those who had been executed and buried them properly.
21.14: They buried Saul and Jonathan in their family tomb in Zelah, in the land of Benjamin. After that, The Most High lifted the famine and answered Israel's prayers.
21.15: The Philistines went to war with Israel again, and David went out to fight—but he got tired fast.
21.16: Ishbi-Benob, one of the giants, saw his chance to kill David. His spear weighed 300 shekels (7.5 pounds), and he had a fresh new sword ready to take David out.
21.17: But Abishai (Joab's brother) jumped in, saved David, and killed the Philistine. After that, David's men told him, 'King, you ain't fightin' no more. If you die, the lamp of Israel goes out.'
21.18: Later, another battle broke out at Gob. Sibbechai the Hushathite killed Saph, another Philistine giant.
21.19: Then another fight happened at Gob. Elhanan from Bethlehem took out Goliath's brother—the one whose spear shaft was thick like a weaver's beam.
21.20: And yet again, there was war at Gath, where they faced a giant with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot—24 digits in total.
21.21: This dude was talkin' reckless, but Jonathan (David's nephew) killed him on sight.
21.22: All four of these giants from Gath got taken out by David and his men.

22.1: David sang this song to The Most High on the day He saved him from all his enemies, including Saul.
22.2: The Lord my rock, my fortress, my way out.
22.3: The God who got my back, the one I put my trust in. My shield, my savior, my stronghold, my safe place. The one who keeps me from harm.
22.4: When I call on The Most High, the one worthy of all praise, I know I'm safe from my enemies.
22.5: Man, death had me surrounded, like waves tryna pull me under.
22.6: I was at my lowest, feelin' trapped, like the grave was closin' in on me.
22.7: But I cried out to The Most High, called on Him in my trouble. He heard me loud and clear from His throne!
22.8: The earth started shakin', the heavens trembled—God was mad!
22.9: Smoke came out His nostrils, fire from His mouth—He was fired up.
22.10: He bent the heavens and came down, darkness under His feet.
22.11: Ridin' on a cherub, flyin' through on the wind.
22.12: He wrapped Himself in darkness, thick clouds all around Him.
22.13: But His brightness still broke through—fire sparkin' from His presence.
22.14: The Most High thundered from the heavens, His voice shook everything!
22.15: He shot His arrows, scatterin' my enemies, sent lightning bolts chasin' 'em down.
22.16: The seas split open, the whole world was laid bare at His rebuke, when He breathed His mighty breath.
22.17: He reached down, grabbed me, and pulled me outta deep waters.
22.18: Saved me from my enemies, from folks way stronger than me.
22.19: They came at me when I was down bad, but The Most High held me up.
22.20: He brought me into a wide-open space, 'cause He got love for me.
22.21: The Most High blessed me 'cause I walked right, 'cause I kept my hands clean.
22.22: I stayed on His path, I ain't turn my back on Him.
22.23: His commands stayed in front of me, and I didn't ignore 'em.
22.24: I kept myself right before Him, I tried to live clean.
22.25: So He blessed me 'cause I stayed faithful, 'cause He saw my heart.
22.26: If you merciful, He gon' show you mercy. If you walk right, He gon' deal with you right.
22.27: If you pure, He gon' be pure with you. But if you shady, He gon' outthink you.
22.28: He lifts up the humble, but He brings down the proud.
22.29: You, Lord, my lamp—You bring light to my darkness.
22.30: With You, I can run through an army, I can jump over walls.
22.31: God's way is perfect, His word never fails. He protects everybody who trusts Him.
22.32: Ain't no god but The Most High, ain't no rock like Him.
22.33: God my strength, my power, the one who makes my path straight.
22.34: He make my feet swift like a deer's, puttin' me on high ground.
22.35: He trains me for battle, makes me strong enough to bend a bronze bow.
22.36: He covers me with His shield of salvation, His care for me lifts me up.
22.37: He made space for me to move, so I ain't trip up.
22.38: I chased my enemies down and wiped 'em out—I ain't stop 'til they were gone.
22.39: I crushed 'em, knocked 'em down, and they couldn't get back up.
22.40: You gave me strength for battle, made my enemies fall at my feet.
22.41: You put their necks under me, and I stomped out those who hated me.
22.42: They cried for help, but nobody saved them. Even The Most High ain't answer them.
22.43: I beat 'em down like dust, stomped 'em out like dirt in the streets.
22.44: You rescued me from my own people's drama and made me ruler over nations.
22.45: Foreigners bowed before me, as soon as they heard my name.
22.46: They lost all courage, hid away like scared men.
22.47: The Most High lives! Blessed be my Rock! Let my God be lifted high!
22.48: He's the one who avenges me, puttin' nations under my rule.
22.49: He saved me from my enemies, lifted me above those who hated me.
22.50: So I'ma thank You, Lord, and sing Your praises to the whole world.
22.51: You my strong tower, showin' mercy to me and my descendants forever.

23.1: These the last words of David, son of Jesse—the man God lifted up, the one He anointed, the songwriter of Israel.
23.2: The Spirit of The Most High spoke through me, and His words stayed on my tongue.
23.3: The God of Israel, the Rock of Israel, told me: 'The one who leads gotta lead with justice, ruling with respect for The Most High.'
23.4: That kind of ruler shines like the sunrise after a storm, like fresh grass growing after the rain.
23.5: Even though my family ain't perfect, God still locked me into a forever promise, securing everything I need. That's my salvation, that's my hope—ain't no way He won't keep blessing me.
23.6: But them rebels? They like thorn bushes—too wild to be grabbed by hand.
23.7: You gotta deal with them using iron and spears, 'cause they gonna end up burned up where they stand.
23.8: These the names of David's top warriors: Josheb-Basshebeth (aka Adino the Eznite), was top of the list—he took out 800 men in one fight.
23.9: Next was Eleazar, son of Dodo—one of the top three warriors. When the Philistines pulled up and Israel's army ran, he stayed.
23.10: He fought so long his hand cramped up around his sword. The Most High gave him victory that day, and when the battle was done, the people only came back to grab the loot.
23.11: Then there was Shammah. The Philistines came trying to take over a field full of lentils, and everybody ran—except him.
23.12: He stood his ground right in the middle of that field, fought 'em off, and The Most High gave him the win.
23.13: One time, three of David's top warriors came down to see him when the Philistines had a camp set up in Bethlehem.
23.14: David was posted up in his stronghold while the Philistines were controlling Bethlehem.
23.15: David sighed and said, 'Man, I'd love some water from that well in Bethlehem by the gate.'
23.16: His three warriors broke through enemy lines, got that water, and brought it back to him.
23.17: But David wouldn't drink it—he poured it out as an offering to The Most High. He said, 'I can't drink this—it's like drinking the blood of the men who risked their lives for it.'
23.18: Abishai, Joab's brother, led another group—he took out 300 men with his spear.
23.19: He was the most respected of that group, but he still wasn't one of the original three.
23.20: Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, was another warrior. He killed two fierce Moabite fighters and even fought a lion in a pit—on a snowy day at that.
23.21: He also fought a giant Egyptian. The Egyptian had a spear, but Benaiah snatched it and killed him with his own weapon.
23.22: Because of this, Benaiah became well-known.
23.23: He was respected more than most, but still not on the level of the top three. David put him in charge of his personal guard.
23.24: Asahel, Joab's brother, was one of the thirty. Elhanan, son of Dodo, was from Bethlehem.
23.25: Shammah the Harodite and Elika the Harodite.
23.26: Helez the Paltite and Ira, son of Ikkesh, from Tekoa.
23.27: Abiezer from Anathoth and Mebunnai the Hushathite.
23.28: Zalmon the Ahohite and Maharai the Netophathite.
23.29: Heleb, son of Baanah, from Netophah. Ittai, son of Ribai, from Gibeah in Benjamin.
23.30: Benaiah the Pirathonite and Hiddai from the brooks of Gaash.
23.31: Abi-Albon the Arbathite and Azmaveth the Barhumite.
23.32: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, one of the sons of Jashen, and Jonathan.
23.33: Shammah the Hararite and Ahiam, son of Sharar, the Hararite.
23.34: Eliphelet, son of Ahasbai, from Maacah, and Eliam, son of Ahithophel, from Giloh.
23.35: Hezrai the Carmelite and Paarai the Arbite.
23.36: Igal, son of Nathan, from Zobah, and Bani the Gadite.
23.37: Zelek the Ammonite and Naharai from Beeroth, Joab's armor-bearer.
23.38: Ira the Ithrite and Gareb the Ithrite.
23.39: Uriah the Hittite. Altogether, 37 mighty warriors.

24.1: The Most High was mad at Israel again, so He let David get caught up in his own thinking. David said, 'Go count everybody in Israel and Judah.'
24.2: David told Joab, his army commander, 'Go through all the tribes, from Dan to Beersheba, and get me the numbers.'
24.3: But Joab wasn't feelin' it. 'May The Most High bless Israel with more people than the stars if He wants, but why you wanna do this, King?'
24.4: David wasn't tryna hear it. So Joab and his officers went out to count the people.
24.5: They traveled the land, crossed the Jordan, camped in Aroer, and hit up the towns in Gad and Jazer.
24.6: Then they went through Gilead, Tahtim Hodshi, Dan Jaan, and around to Sidon.
24.7: They came to the stronghold of Tyre, checked in on all the Hivites and Canaanites, then went south to Judah, all the way to Beersheba.
24.8: After nine months and twenty days of counting, they made it back to Jerusalem.
24.9: Joab handed David the numbers: 800,000 warriors in Israel, 500,000 in Judah.
24.10: Soon as the numbers came in, David's heart hit him hard. 'Man, I really messed up. The Most High, please forgive me—I did something real foolish.'
24.11: The next morning, The Most High sent a word to the prophet Gad, David's seer.
24.12: 'Tell David he got three choices—pick one.'
24.13: So Gad told David, 'You want seven years of famine, three months of runnin' from your enemies, or three days of a deadly plague? Think on it.'
24.14: David was shook. 'I can't pick… but I'd rather fall into The Most High's hands than man's, 'cause God got mercy.'
24.15: The Most High sent a plague that lasted three days, and 70,000 people died from Dan to Beersheba.
24.16: The angel of The Most High stretched his hand over Jerusalem, ready to destroy it—but The Most High stopped him. 'That's enough. Pull back.' The angel stood by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
24.17: David saw the angel and cried out, 'I'm the one who sinned, not them! Let the punishment be on me and my family.'
24.18: Gad came to David and told him, 'Go to Araunah's threshing floor and build an altar there.'
24.19: David did exactly what The Most High commanded.
24.20: Araunah looked up and saw the king and his servants coming. He bowed low before David, face to the ground.
24.22: David said, 'I need to buy this land to build an altar, so The Most High will take this plague off the people.'
24.23: Araunah was like, 'Take whatever you need! Use my oxen for sacrifices, my wood for the fire—everything's yours!'
24.24: But David said, 'Nah, I gotta pay for it. I can't offer The Most High something that cost me nothing.'
24.25: So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver. Then he built an altar, made offerings, and prayed. The Most High answered, and the plague stopped.
